outcome: Transfers (pre-32 weeks, post-32 weeks, perinatal, postnatal, newborn)
cohort: The study included 2,448 pregnant women who received care at the Outaouais Birthing Center between 2016 and 2023.
finding: COVID-19 did not increase the overall prevalence of GBS colonization in pregnant women, but was associated with a temporary spike in 2020 and notable changes in newborn and postnatal transfers and Apgar scores, suggesting an influence on healthcare practices.
